audits.text:
## 7781a5e94155

**Reproduced generator-domain defect: single-pixel-only scenes collapse object
segmentation into a pixel shortcut.**

At seed `0`, sample index `0`, difficulty `medium`, the current generator emits a
validator-clean connected polyomino in which every nonzero color occurs at one
pixel. A rival that treats each nonzero pixel as its own object, sorts pixels by
`(column,row)`, and outputs pixel-cardinal adjacency exactly matches the selected
Racket output on this generated case.

Canonical train pair 0 contains multi-cell monochrome objects. The same rival
then produces a `7×7` pixel graph instead of the authority's `3×3` object graph,
and the current `self_check` rejects the canonical input because colors 4, 2,
and 3 occur more than once. Thus the documented generated domain omits the
abstraction the task requires and makes a wrong pixel-level rule exact.

Evidence: `checks/audit/7781a5e94155/case.json` (case SHA-256
`7f6fd68ddc336687722911e215d1ad84ab786cb58adc5b21d054cb9d29d32858`),
with supported authority transcript at
`checks/audit/7781a5e94155/racket.json`. Generator SHA-256 is
`c545db1edf02cbed2b4c7671eaae76c60cdcd14ab9083a62f41c7f7b8797fbbe`;
rule hash is `b98ae53ca23e`. No patch was made because this is audit-only.

## 7781a5e94155

**Reproduced defect: the generator teaches a pixel-as-object shortcut and excludes canonical multi-cell objects.** The assigned/current generator SHA-256 was `c545db1edf02cbed2b4c7671eaae76c60cdcd14ab9083a62f41c7f7b8797fbbe`.

The scoped audit found no task-local tests and failed the semantic gate because the generator declares no strict/semantic/lesson contract. A fresh source-bound witness then compared the selected Racket rule with the rival “treat each nonzero pixel as its own object, sort by `(column,row)`, and emit pixel-cardinal adjacency.” The generated default-domain replay `{seed: 0, sample_index: 0, difficulty: medium}` passes `self_check`, and the rival matches the selected Racket output exactly. Canonical train pair 0 contains multi-cell monochrome objects; `self_check` rejects it because colors 4, 2, and 3 appear more than once, and the same rival produces a different 7×7 output instead of the authoritative 3×3 output.

This is not merely a missing declaration: the generated domain removes the object-connectivity distinction needed to learn the canonical rule. The complete witness, replay, outputs, domain verdict, source/rule hashes, and evidence links are in `checks/audit/7781a5e94155/case.json` (SHA-256 `f9077f864d34aba1f60ddb891e0735948ea5ec0e60930b82e39956a1d43a18f9`); selected-rule execution is in `checks/audit/7781a5e94155/racket.json`. The failing audit receipt is `checks/audit/7781a5e94155-combined/checks/7781a5e94155_audit_semantic_gate.json`.

No patch was made because this was an audit-only target. Recommended repair: generate connected monochrome objects with variable area/shape, accept canonical multi-cell inputs, declare the pixel rival and object-connectivity witnesses, and retain a Racket-labelled generated counterexample before training admission.
